chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I saw Abu Ja'far عليه السلام perform salat in a single waist-wrapper that was not wide, which he had tied over his neck. So I said to him: What do you consider regarding a man performing salat in a single shirt? He said: “If it is thick, then there is no harm in it. And a woman performs salat in a shift and a head-covering if the shift is thick,” meaning, “if it is concealing.” I said: May Allah have mercy on you, does the bondwoman cover her head when she performs salat? He said: “There is no head-covering required upon the bondwoman.”

key_terms.إِزَارٍ: a waist-wrapper or lower garment worn for covering the body
key_terms.الدِّرْعِ: a woman's shift or long garment worn in prayer
key_terms.الْمِقْنَعَةِ: a head-covering worn by a woman
key_terms.سَتِيرًا: concealing, providing proper coverage of the body
key_terms.قَمِيصٍ: a shirt or tunic worn as a single garment in prayer
key_terms.كَثِيفًا: thick enough not to reveal what is beneath it

ai.seo_question: What clothing is sufficient for a man or woman to wear in salat according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal rulings of clothing worn during salat, focusing on whether a single garment is sufficient if it is thick and concealing. It also distinguishes between the dress requirements of a free woman and a bondwoman in prayer.
